title: Small multiples instead of one overloaded chart

videos.script: Five regions, twenty-four months, one chart. Five coloured lines. {{five}} The top line is easy. The others tangle, cross, and hide behind each other. To follow one region, you have to find its colour in the legend, then find the line, then follow it through every crossing. {{tangle}} Now split the chart. One small chart per region, side by side, all on the same scale. {{split}} Each line has a panel to itself. You read the shape of every region at once, without a legend and without a single crossing. And because the scale is shared, the comparisons still work: Southeast sits high, North sits low. {{panels}} Edward Tufte called this small multiples. The same chart repeated, with one thing changing between the copies. {{tufte}} In this lesson you build them, you decide when the scales should be shared, and you choose the order of the panels. {{plan}}
